question: How are rental fees calculated for public market stalls, and what surcharges apply to front corner booths?
answer:
The rental fees for public market stalls are calculated based on the class of the stall and the size, as specified in the City Treasurer's CGD_Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II-2.pdf [S1, S2, S3].

For Class A, the rate per square meter per day is P 4. For Class B, it's P 6, for Class C, P 4, and for Class D, P 2. If a stall is a front corner stall or booth, a 20% surcharge will be added to the prescribed fees [S2]. If it's a front stall or booth, a 15% surcharge will be added [S2]. For inside corner stalls or booths, a 10% surcharge will be added [S2].

There is also an automatic increase of 15% every four years, computed based on the existing rates of fees to the increasing cost of maintenance operations [S2].

For delinquency in paying the monthly rentals for market stalls, a surcharge of twenty-five pesos (P 25) per day is applicable after the 20th day of the month [S3].

ground_truth: Public market rental rates vary by classification and section (e.g., Meat Class A is PHP 40.00/sq.m./day; Class D is PHP 13.50). Additional location surcharges apply: 20% for front corner stalls, 15% for front stalls, and 10% for inside corner stalls.
